scope: Around each city outside the UK, schools are mapped inside the same rectangle as the city’s crime data, and only in the city’s own state, province or entity. So a city’s schools can include neighbouring towns in that state: around New York City they include Yonkers, Mount Vernon and New Rochelle in Westchester County, and towns in western Nassau County such as Valley Stream and Great Neck.

Missouri does not publish an overall rating for each of its schools.
Minnesota does not publish a single overall rating for its schools.

Offers credits toward the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD), according to the Ministry of Education's private school list. The Ministry inspects the OSSD credit courses of private high schools and lets them grant credits only after a successful inspection; it does not inspect premises, health and safety or staffing. Ontario's Ministry of Education does not license, accredit or endorse private schools, and publishes no rating for them.

Ontario publishes no single school rating or inspection grade for its publicly funded schools. Its testing agency, EQAO, publishes provincial test results separately; they are not a rating and are not shown here.

No official rating is published for this private school. US private schools come from NCES’s 2023-24 Private School Universe Survey, which lists only the schools that answered it (about 3 in 4), so some private schools are not on this map.

Mexico does not publish an official rating or inspection result for individual schools. PLANEA, the national test whose results were published school by school, was last given in 2019 in lower-secondary schools and in 2022 in upper-secondary schools, and it has not been replaced by any school rating. Mejoredu, the federal body that evaluated education, was abolished by a constitutional reform in December 2024.

us-az-af.title: Arizona school letter grade (ADE)
us-az-af.scale: A (highest) to F. "Not rated" (NR) means the school does not have the parts of ADE’s model needed to receive a grade.
us-az-af.measures: Mostly state test proficiency and growth; high schools also count graduation and college and career readiness.
us-az-af.caveat: This is the Arizona Department of Education’s official A–F letter grade for the 2024-25 school year, as published on its AZ School Report Cards site. Alternative schools are graded under a separate model.
us-az-af.publisher: Arizona Department of Education (AZ School Report Cards)
us-az-af.attribution: Arizona Department of Education, AZ School Report Cards (2024-25 letter grades).
us-az-af.miss: {place} publishes this letter grade, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-ca-essa.title: California federal support status (CDE)
us-ca-essa.short: ESSA assistance status — not a rating
us-ca-essa.scale: California does not give schools an overall rating. Under the federal Every Student Succeeds Act it identifies some schools for support: Comprehensive (CSI), Targeted (TSI) or Additional Targeted (ATSI) Support and Improvement. Most schools are not identified.
us-ca-essa.measures: Identification comes from the California School Dashboard indicators (test results, graduation, chronic absence, suspensions, English learner progress, college and career readiness).
us-ca-essa.caveat: This is not a rating. The Dashboard reports each indicator separately and does not combine them.
us-ca-essa.attribution: California Department of Education, 2025-26 ESSA Assistance Status data file.
values: Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI): low performance
Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI): low graduation rate
us-ca-essa.miss: {place} publishes this status for its public schools, but this school is not in its {year} file.

notes.html: See the California School Dashboard ↗ for the separate indicators.

us-co-spf.title: Colorado school plan type (CDE)
us-co-spf.scale: Performance, Improvement, Priority Improvement or Turnaround plan (Performance is highest). It sets the kind of improvement plan a school must file; it is a planning category, not a grade.
us-co-spf.measures: State test (CMAS, PSAT and SAT) achievement and growth and, for high schools, graduation, dropout and college matriculation rates.
us-co-spf.caveat: These 2026 ratings are preliminary and may still change through Colorado’s request-to-reconsider process; final ratings are expected at the end of 2026.
us-co-spf.attribution: Colorado Department of Education, 2026 Preliminary School Performance Framework ratings.
values: Improvement Plan: Decreased due to Participation
Priority Improvement Plan: Decreased due to Participation
Turnaround Plan: Decreased due to Participation
Insufficient State Data: Small Tested Population
Insufficient State Data: No Students at Grade Levels Tested for State Assessments
us-co-spf.miss: {place} publishes this plan type, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

notes.html: "AEC" means an Alternative Education Campus, rated on a separate framework.

us-ct-ngas.title: Connecticut accountability category (CSDE)
us-ct-ngas.scale: Category 1 (highest) to Category 5. Categories 1 to 3 follow the school’s accountability index; schools identified for state support (Focus or Turnaround) are in Categories 4 and 5.
us-ct-ngas.measures: Twelve indicators: test achievement and growth, attendance, graduation, college and career readiness, arts access and physical fitness.
us-ct-ngas.caveat: A lower category number is better.
us-ct-ngas.attribution: Connecticut State Department of Education, Next Generation Accountability System 2024-25 (data.ct.gov).
us-ct-ngas.miss: {place} publishes this category, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-dc-score.title: DC School Report Card score (OSSE)
us-dc-score.scale: Points out of 100 on the District of Columbia’s school accountability framework.
us-dc-score.measures: State test achievement and growth, chronic absence and attendance growth, re-enrollment, English learner progress, pre-K classroom observations and, for high schools, graduation, SAT and advanced coursework.
us-dc-score.caveat: DC no longer publishes star ratings.
us-dc-score.publisher: Office of the State Superintendent of Education (OSSE)
us-dc-score.attribution: Office of the State Superintendent of Education, DC School Report Card Accountability Scores (2025).
us-dc-score.miss: OSSE’s {year} file gives this school no overall School Score. Early-childhood and early-grade campuses are often scored on only part of the framework and given no overall score, and alternative, adult and special education settings are often not scored.

us-il-sd.title: Illinois summative designation (ISBE)
us-il-sd.scale: Exemplary (top 10%), Commendable, Targeted, Comprehensive or Intensive; the last three mean the school is identified for support.
us-il-sd.measures: State test proficiency and growth, English learner progress, chronic absence, graduation, ninth-grade on-track and school climate.
us-il-sd.attribution: Illinois State Board of Education, 2025 Report Card Public Data Set.
us-il-sd.miss: {place} publishes this designation, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.
us-il-sd.vintage: 2025 (ISBE Report Card Public Data Set, General)

us-la-sps.title: Louisiana school letter grade (LDOE)
us-la-sps.scale: A (highest) to F, from the school’s School Performance Score.
us-la-sps.measures: Mostly state test achievement and progress; high schools also count ACT results, strength of diploma and graduation.
us-la-sps.caveat: Alternative schools are graded with a separate formula and are marked as such.
us-la-sps.attribution: Louisiana Department of Education, 2025 School Performance Scores.
us-la-sps.miss: {place} publishes this letter grade, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-ma-class.title: Massachusetts accountability classification (DESE)
us-ma-class.scale: Schools are "Not requiring assistance or intervention" (from School of Recognition and meeting targets down to limited or no progress) or "Requiring assistance or intervention" (focused/targeted or broad/comprehensive support).
us-ma-class.measures: Progress toward state targets on test achievement and growth, English learner progress, chronic absence, graduation and advanced coursework.
us-ma-class.caveat: Based on progress toward targets, not a ranking.
us-ma-class.publisher: Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education
us-ma-class.attribution: Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education, 2026 Accountability Determinations.
values: Not requiring assistance or intervention: School of Recognition
Not requiring assistance or intervention: Meeting or exceeding targets
Not requiring assistance or intervention: Substantial progress toward targets
Not requiring assistance or intervention: Moderate progress toward targets
Not requiring assistance or intervention: Limited or no progress toward targets
Requiring assistance or intervention: In need of focused/targeted support
Requiring assistance or intervention: In need of broad/comprehensive support
us-ma-class.miss: {place} publishes this classification, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-md-stars.title: Maryland school star rating (MSDE)
us-md-stars.short: Maryland School Report Card star rating
us-md-stars.scale: 1 to 5 stars (5 is highest), set by the share of possible points the school earned.
us-md-stars.measures: Academic indicators (test achievement and progress, graduation, English learner progress) make up 65% of the points; school quality and student success measures, such as chronic absence, make up 35%.
us-md-stars.attribution: Maryland State Department of Education, Maryland Report Card 2025 Accountability Schools.
us-md-stars.miss: {place} publishes this star rating, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-mi-index.title: Michigan School Index (MDE)
us-mi-index.scale: An index from 0 to 100. Where Michigan also identifies the school for federal support (Comprehensive, Targeted or Additional Targeted), that is shown after the index.
us-mi-index.measures: Growth, proficiency, graduation, English learner progress, school quality (such as attendance) and test participation.
us-mi-index.attribution: Michigan Department of Education, 2024-25 School Index Results.
us-mi-index.miss: {place} publishes this index, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-nc-spg.title: North Carolina School Performance Grade (NCDPI)
us-nc-spg.measures: Mostly achievement: 80% is test scores and other achievement measures, 20% is student growth.
us-nc-spg.caveat: Grades closely track how many students are from low-income families.
us-nc-spg.publisher: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction
us-nc-spg.attribution: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, School Report Card data set 2024-25 (School Performance Grades).
us-nc-spg.miss: {place} publishes this grade, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-nv-nspf.title: Nevada school star rating (NSPF)
us-nv-nspf.short: Nevada School Performance Framework star rating
us-nv-nspf.scale: 1 to 5 stars (5 is highest), rated separately for each school level (elementary, middle, high) a school serves.
us-nv-nspf.measures: State test proficiency and growth, closing opportunity gaps, English learner progress, attendance and, for high schools, graduation and college and career readiness.
us-nv-nspf.caveat: "Not rated" means Nevada gave that level no stars (0 in its file).
us-nv-nspf.attribution: Nevada Department of Education, Nevada Report Card, NSPF Disaggregated Data File (2026).
us-nv-nspf.miss: {place} publishes this star rating, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-ny-essa.title: New York federal accountability status (NYSED)
us-ny-essa.short: ESSA accountability status — not a rating
us-ny-essa.scale: Under the federal Every Student Succeeds Act, New York identifies some schools for extra support: Comprehensive (CSI), Targeted (TSI) or Additional Targeted (ATSI) Support and Improvement. Most schools are in "Local Support and Improvement", meaning they are not identified.
us-ny-essa.measures: Identification uses state test performance and growth, graduation, English language proficiency progress, chronic absence and college, career and civic readiness.
us-ny-essa.attribution: New York State Education Department, 2025-26 NYS Accountability Statuses.
us-ny-essa.miss: {place} publishes this status for its public schools, but this school is not in its {year} file.

us-oh-stars.title: Ohio Overall Star Rating (Ohio School Report Cards)
us-oh-stars.scale: 1 to 5 stars in half-star steps (5 is highest).
us-oh-stars.measures: Achievement, progress (growth), gap closing, early literacy, graduation and college, career, workforce and military readiness, weighted together.
us-oh-stars.caveat: Dropout-recovery schools get a separate report card with different measures; their stars are marked as such.
us-oh-stars.publisher: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
us-oh-stars.attribution: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce, Ohio School Report Cards 2025-26 data download.
us-oh-stars.miss: {place} publishes this star rating, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-pa-essa.title: Pennsylvania federal school designation (PDE)
us-pa-essa.short: ESSA school designation — not a rating
us-pa-essa.scale: Under the federal Every Student Succeeds Act, Pennsylvania designates some schools for support: CSI (among the lowest-performing Title I schools, or a low graduation rate), A-TSI or TSI (one or more student groups performing at or below set levels), and ACSI (A-TSI schools that did not meet exit criteria within 4 years). Most schools have no designation.
us-pa-essa.measures: Designations come from the Future Ready PA Index: state test proficiency and growth, graduation, English learner progress and chronic absence.
us-pa-essa.attribution: Pennsylvania Department of Education, Future Ready PA Index, School Fast Facts 2024-25.
us-pa-essa.miss: {place} publishes this designation for its public schools, but this school is not in its {year} file.

us-tn-af.title: Tennessee school letter grade (TDOE)
us-tn-af.scale: A (highest) to F. A school with too few tested students is "Not Eligible for a Letter Grade".
us-tn-af.measures: Half of the grade is achievement on state tests; most of the rest is student growth, and high schools also count college and career readiness.
us-tn-af.attribution: Tennessee Department of Education, 2024-25 A-F Letter Grade File.
values: Not Eligible for a Letter Grade
us-tn-af.miss: {place} publishes this letter grade, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-tx-af.title: Texas school rating (TEA)
us-tx-af.scale: A (highest) to F, or Not Rated.
us-tx-af.measures: Mostly STAAR test results (achievement, progress and closing gaps between student groups); high schools also count graduation and college, career and military readiness.
us-tx-af.caveat: 2026 ratings can still change on appeal. Alternative-education campuses are rated under different rules. Rating data © Texas Education Agency.
us-tx-af.attribution: © Texas Education Agency, 2026 statewide multi-year ratings.
us-tx-af.licence: © Texas Education Agency (TEA copyright notice; shown with attribution and a link, by owner decision)
us-tx-af.miss: {place} publishes this rating, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.

us-wa-wsif.title: Washington School Improvement Framework (OSPI)
us-wa-wsif.scale: Foundational supports (not identified), or identified for support: Tier 1 (one or two student groups), Tier 2 (three or more groups) or Tier 3 (all students, or a low graduation rate). The score runs from 1 to 10.
us-wa-wsif.measures: State test proficiency and growth, graduation, English learner progress, regular attendance, ninth-grade on-track and dual credit.
us-wa-wsif.caveat: Each measure is scored by decile among Washington schools, so the score shows where a school stands among them; it is not a percentage. Data from OSPI under CC BY 4.0; tier labels lightly reworded.
us-wa-wsif.publisher: Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction
us-wa-wsif.attribution: Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction, Washington School Improvement Framework 2025 (data.wa.gov); labels lightly reworded by SafeRoute.
us-wa-wsif.miss: {place} publishes this tier, but has none for this school in its {year} file. Special education, alternative, pre-K and career centres are often not rated.
